segments.title: Setting up the recording at the library
segments.summary: Mic checks, names and date (May 15, 1975), and restarting the tape before the playback session.

segments.title: Starting the record with clarinet breaks; an international record
segments.summary: Davenport explains opening the tune with breaks; Wood describes the record as made with an English band, cut in Germany and finished in New Orleans, due out soon.

segments.title: Playing with the radio-studio musicians in Vienna
segments.summary: Davenport recalls the excellent Vienna musicians who backed him, a symphony drummer and radio-studio players.

segments.title: Where chase choruses came from
segments.summary: The group discusses the origin of trading fours; Davenport ties it to jam sessions like prize fights, Wood to the Chicago crowd and older records.

segments.title: Playing back a number the band rehearsed
segments.summary: Phone interruption and mic handling while a rehearsed number is played; a Blue Note-era traditional tune is praised.

segments.title: Frog on trombone, Bob Martin's accent, and keeping the tradition
segments.summary: Talk of Frog struggling with the bridge, the British band's musicianship, Bob Martin's accent when singing Sister Kate, and adding new things while keeping tradition.

segments.title: Rewinding the tape; the trombone hole and Davenport as thorough
segments.summary: The tune announcement, the space left for the trombone and bass overdubs, tape handling, and Wood calling Davenport thorough.

segments.title: Hating to leave the European band; playing I Can't Stop Loving You his own way
segments.summary: Davenport enjoyed two weeks with the band and contrasts it with playing set arrangements with Basie and Ray Charles.

segments.title: Rock musicians, jazz musicians and what a bandleader expects
segments.summary: Davenport and Wood discuss how young rock players decide together, and how hired players should follow the leader.

segments.title: Explaining bass lines to a trombone player
segments.summary: Davenport describes playing roots and fifths and starting chords on the root, advising listening to classical music.

segments.title: Breaking the tempo in half at the ending
segments.summary: Davenport explains how he got the band to halve the tempo after the drum break; quick to understand.

segments.title: Louis Armstrong's influence and the trumpet lineage
segments.summary: Davenport says he phrased like Armstrong on his solo, and traces trumpet influence through Eldridge, Gillespie, Miles Davis and Parker.

segments.title: Clifford Brown phrasing in his solo; Bill Bailey overdub reaction
segments.summary: Davenport notes Armstrong and Clifford Brown phrases in the solo; Wood recalls the studio reaction when trombone and bass were dubbed on Bill Bailey.

segments.title: Library announcements and tape noise
segments.summary: Library closing announcement and degraded repetitive transcript while the tape continues.

segments.title: Navy concert band and lessons with Gilbert Mitchell
segments.summary: Davenport recalls the Navy symphonic band and studying privately with Gilbert Mitchell in 1945 before Xavier.

segments.title: Learning timing from Professor Tull
segments.summary: Davenport credits Professor Tull's down-left-right-up counting method for his timing; the interviewer says his teacher Manetta taught the same.

segments.title: Library closing and tape repair
segments.summary: The library announces closing and they fuss over a piece of tape on the machine.

segments.title: The interviewer's verdict on the album
segments.summary: Davenport asks what the interviewer thought; he calls it the best he has heard Wallace play, praising the team understanding.

segments.title: Packing up and release form
segments.summary: Packing tapes, a signed release, and locking up.
